clue.text: Girl holding up computer manufacturer's re-animated remains

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the maker's initials inside it, splitting after its second letter

parts.note: Zoe is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: IBM is the American computer company

explanation.surface: A girl props up the reanimated remains of some computer firm's product.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads backwards; 'holding' splits the girl's name round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A zombie in folklore is a corpse brought back to a semblance of life.

clue.text: Plunging top to toe into metal 1s

definitions.note: refers to the answer to 1 down, plural: the walking dead

indicators.note: the reworked plunging word goes into the metal, right after its first letter

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal

indicators.note: the top letter of the word is moved down to its foot, its last place

parts.note: diving means plunging

explanation.surface: Diving head first into heavy metal turns people into zombies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top to toe' sends the first letter to the end; 'into' places the result after the L of the metal. '1s' means 1 Down, made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Zombies are the classic undead, corpses that walk as if alive, hence the phrase for them.

clue.text: Like ancient poet's photo capturing faulty drain

indicators.note: the photo word takes the rearranged letters into its middle

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo

indicators.note: a faulty drain is broken, so its letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A photograph shows a broken drain in classical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' gives INDAR; 'capturing' wraps the picture round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pindar was the ancient Greek lyric poet of odes, and the adjective describes his style.

clue.text: Share prayer, wanting nothing

indicators.note: wanting here means lacking, so the zero is taken away

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech or prayer
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone shares a prayer but gets nothing back.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed allowance or portion given out is a share of something scarce.

clue.text: Vagabond to smuggle mineral

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them
agate is a banded quartz mineral

explanation.surface: A tramp is set to sneak a gemstone past customs.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a wanderer or deserter, a roving vagrant.

clue.text: Turtle's head fit for consumption — on this?

definitions.text: Turtle's head fit for consumption — on this?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: eatable means fit to be eaten

explanation.surface: Turtle's head is ready to eat: where would it be served?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: food fit for consumption is laid on such a piece of furniture at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: A small table at which afternoon tea and its food are served.

clue.text: Endless wine Shed's knocked back with officiant

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is knocked back, read in reverse order
endless means the wine loses its final letter

parts.note: retsina is a resinated Greek wine
Shed is the setter, so Shed's means I am, contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: The setter downs a bottle of wine, finishing it off, alongside a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last A; 'knocked back' reverses the whole string RETSINIM. Shed is this puzzle's setter, so 'Shed's' means I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman who conducts services officiates at them.

clue.text: Plenty of mucus around

indicators.note: around signals turning the word round, reading it backwards

parts.note: snot is slang for nasal mucus

explanation.surface: There's mucus everywhere, and lots of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a great quantity of something is a lot, loads.

clue.text: Smell smoke

definitions.meaning: to stink, give off a strong odour
Scottish and dialect sense: to give off smoke or vapour

explanation.definitionFit: Both a strong unpleasant odour and, in older use, the act of emitting smoke or fumes.

clue.text: Close bank experiencing setback in US city

indicators.note: the reversed bank sits within the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: a setback sends the word backwards

parts.note: brae is a Scottish word for a hillside or bank

explanation.surface: A local bank is having troubles in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experiencing setback' turns BRAE to EARB, put 'in' NY. Brae is Scots for a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is within a short distance.

clue.text: Getting shot of free fling

parts.note: to rid is to free
a fling is a lively dance, as in the Highland fling

explanation.surface: Ending a carefree affair means getting shot of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rid of something unwanted, as in good riddance, is getting shot of it.

clue.text: Character in Hamlet attended wild parties, bumping into popular performer?

indicators.note: the party word bumps its way into the middle of the performer

parts.note: a gigger is one who plays gigs, a pop musician
to rave is to go to wild dance parties

explanation.surface: A Hamlet actor went partying and collided with a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popular performer' is a pop musician who plays gigs; the surface hides that a role, not an actor, is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The clown who digs Ophelia's grave and unearths Yorick's skull is a role in the play.

clue.text: 1's interrupting one Asian or another

indicators.note: the numeral word breaks into the middle of the nationality

parts.note: an Indian is one Asian national
the figure 1 read as a word, plural: ones

explanation.surface: A digit cuts into one Asian nationality or another.
explanation.walkthrough: '1's' is the plain digit made plural, not a reference to 1 Down; 'interrupting' breaks into the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Indonesia is a further Asian national beside the Indian, so another one.

clue.text: Old exclamation about … about falling water … or how to get rid of it?

definitions.text: how to get rid of it?

indicators.note: the second about means the turned exclamation goes around the water
the first about turns the exclamation round, reading it backwards

parts.note: egad is an old oath, a mild form of by God
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: An old cry about rain: what to do about the falling water?
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'about' reverses the oath to DAGE; the second wraps it round the falling water.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipes and ditches carry away surplus water, the system for clearing it.

clue.text: Most overpriced fly mostly securing piss-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the whole assembly to read from the bottom
the trimmed fly holds the urine word inside it
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: the tsetse is an African biting fly
pee is a milder word for piss

explanation.surface: A fly drinks at the most expensive boozy session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' gives TSETS; 'securing' makes TSEPEETS; 'up' reverses the lot. 'piss-up' is British slang for a drinking session, split here.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is informal for excessively priced, so the superlative is costing most.

clue.text: Designer of hobbit, elf or dwarf?

indicators.note: the designer's name is taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Who created the hobbit, the elf or the dwarf?
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas TELFORD was the Scottish civil engineer who designed bridges and canals; the surface sends you to Tolkien.
explanation.definitionFit: The engineer drew up plans for roads, canals and bridges, a builder of works.

clue.text: Revolutionary or mordant?

parts.note: mordant wit is biting, sharp

explanation.surface: Is the speaker a radical, or just sarcastic?
explanation.definitionFit: Going round and round in a circuit, as planets do, is revolving.

clue.text: It's not the whole story, but recipe's included

indicators.note: the abbreviation is included within the word for but

parts.note: except means but, as in all but one
R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: It's only a partial account, but at least the recipe is in.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract or passage taken from a longer text is only part of it.

clue.text: Monk's live number accommodating rule

parts.note: to be is to live, exist

indicators.note: the number takes the rule into its middle

parts.note: nine is a number
an edict is a decree or rule

explanation.surface: A monk's lively issue is accommodating the rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monk's' reads as Monk is, so the 's is a link. 'accommodating' has NINE take in EDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother of the order founded by St Benedict.

clue.text: High point? No more than 151

parts.note: in Roman numerals 151 is C (100), L (50) and I (1)
max, maximum, means no more than

explanation.surface: Is the peak a mere one hundred and fifty-one at most?
explanation.definitionFit: The culmination or peak of something, its most intense moment.

clue.text: Letters from louse unopened

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: aphis is the genus of aphid, a plant louse

explanation.surface: Letters arrive from someone despicable, still sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'louse' is the plant louse, APHIS, not a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the 21st letter of the Greek alphabet; the plural means several such characters.

clue.text: Down and dirty

explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means both depressed in mood and risqué, as with jokes or films.

clue.text: Oil the wheels with S&M … and bondage?

indicators.note: wheels means turns around, rolling the letters into a new order

parts.note: the two letters S and M

explanation.surface: Lubricate things with sadomasochism and restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' rearranges only OIL THE; the S and M stay at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Serfdom, as of the helots, the state serfs of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: River drowning one Roman governor

indicators.note: the river drowns the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: the River Plate in South America
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A river drowns a Roman governor.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside PLATE after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontius Pilate was the Roman prefect of Judaea who tried Jesus.

clue.text: Instrument-maker's to stop drinking wine when drunk

indicators.note: the stopping word drinks the jumbled wine, taking it inside

parts.note: to stay is to stop, remain

indicators.note: drunk means rearranged, the letters staggering

explanation.surface: A piano maker must give up drinking wine once drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' rearranges WINE to EINW; 'drinking' puts it inside. The 's after the definition means is.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinway & Sons is the famous New York piano manufacturer.

clue.text: Yearn to introduce soldiers to Mum or Dad

indicators.note: the yearning word introduces the soldiers into its middle

parts.note: to pant for something is to yearn for it
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: A woman longs to introduce soldiers to her parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Either a mother or a father, so one of the two who raise a child.
